messages.content: Which file wins when a submitter resends the same day?

The resend with the later timestamp in the file name wins. Parse the `YYYYMMDD_HHMM` part of the name and order descending; the file with the highest `HHMM` for that business date is the one that supersedes earlier copies (and if timestamps tie, use the lexically greater name)【4】.

<context>
<passage id="1" source="incidents/INC-0438-mobile-column-rename.md" section="Fix">
INC-0438: MOBILE file renamed a dedup-key column | Fix
Submitter resent with the contracted header at 11:05 the same day. The day was reprocessed; the null-key rows were superseded by the resend under latest-file-wins.
</passage>

<passage id="2" source="runbooks/backfills-and-reprocessing.md" section="Reprocessing a day">
Backfills and reprocessing | Reprocessing a day
1. Land the corrected file (resend) with a later `HHMM` in the file name so latest-file-wins picks it up.
2. Trigger `retail_txn_daily` for the business date with `reprocess=true`. This re-runs dedupe and both dbt models for that date only.
3. Check `publish_metrics` output against the file trailer counts.
4. Write a ledger entry with the incident id, the date range, and who approved it.
</passage>

<passage id="3" source="runbooks/volume-anomalies.md" section="Fix">
Volume anomalies | Fix
Truncated file: request a full resend, then reprocess the day. Stores offline: no fix needed in the pipeline, but annotate the day so the trailing average for next week is not dragged down.
</passage>

<passage id="4" source="runbooks/submitter-onboarding.md" section="Resends">
Submitter files and naming convention | Resends
A resend uses the same date and a later `HHMM`. Submitters must not reuse a file name; the loader rejects a name it has already seen.
</passage>

<passage id="5" source="runbooks/duplicate-submissions.md" section="Overview">
Duplicate submissions and the latest-file-wins rule | Overview
Submitters resend files. Sometimes it is a correction, sometimes an operator re-ran an export by mistake. Either way the same transaction lands twice and naive totals double count.
</passage>
